title: Topological rationality of immediate one-dimensional analytic fields
statement: Let $k\subseteq E$ be complete fields with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, with $k$ algebraically closed [def-weil-field]. For any such field $F$ put $F^\circ=\{a:|a|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{a:|a|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|\subset\mathbf R_{>0}$. For $z\in E$ write $k(z)^\wedge$ for the closure of the subfield generated by $k$ and $z$. Assume $E\ne k$ and $E$ is finite over $k(y)^\wedge$ for some $y\in E$. Assume $\widetilde E=\widetilde k$ and $\Gamma_E=\Gamma_k$ (an immediate extension). Then there exists $z\in E\setminus k$ such that $E=k(z)^\wedge$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1(i), type 4 argument, printed p. 50, specialized to algebraically closed k: every finite extension is immediate, and the proof constructs a topological generator.

proof.text:
Put $K_0=k(y)^\wedge$. Since $E
e k$ and $[E:K_0]<\infty$, we have $y
otin k$: otherwise every element of $E$ would be algebraic over the algebraically closed field $k$, hence in $k$. The residue and value groups of $K_0$, as subobjects of those of $E$, lie between the equal ones of $k$ and $E$ and therefore equal those of $k$. Every intermediate field in $E/K_0$ is complete by [lem-per-finite-normed-space-complete], applied to its inherited norm and its finite dimension over the complete field $K_0$. The closed subfield $K_0$ itself is complete, since it is a closed subset of the complete metric field $E$. By [lem-trf-analytic-type-alternatives], $\widetilde k$ is algebraically closed and $\Gamma_k$ divisible. Apply [lem-trf-analytic-ramification-tower] to $E/K_0$. In residue characteristic zero it gives $E=K_0$, so $z=y$ works. In residue characteristic $p>0$ it gives $K_0\subset\cdots\subset K_n=E$ with every successive degree $p$. We induct on $i$ that $K_i=k(z_i)^\wedge$ with $z_i
otin k$, starting with $z_0=y$. Every $K_i/k$ is immediate by the same inclusions of residue fields and value groups.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, p. 50, reduction to degree p; completeness hypotheses made explicit.

proof.text: For the induction step put $K=K_i$ and $L=K_{i+1}$. These are complete, $[L:K]=p$, and both are immediate over $k$. By [lem-trf-analytic-prime-coset-model] choose $a,s,b$ and the special coset $C=b+S_{a,s}(K)$ split over $L$. By [lem-trf-analytic-coset-generator-reduction], choose $v\in C$ with $v\in k$ or $K=k(v)^\wedge$. The constant case is impossible: $T^p-aT+v$ has a root $c\in k\subset K$ by algebraic closedness, whereas the model asserts $s=\inf_{c\in K}|c^p-ac+v|>0$. Thus $K=k(v)^\wedge$ and $v\notin k$. The model applies to this actual representative $v$, giving $|pv|<s$ and the splitting element in $L$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, p. 50, normalized representative; constant exclusion simplified using algebraic closedness.

proof.text: If $a=1$, the model gives $\alpha\in L$ with $\alpha^p-\alpha+v=0$ and $L=K(\alpha)$. Put $H=k(\alpha)^\wedge\subset L$. The identity $v=-\alpha^p+\alpha$ implies $K=k(v)^\wedge\subset H$, so $L=K(\alpha)\subset H\subset L$ and $H=L$. Moreover $\alpha\notin k$ since otherwise $v\in k$. This completes this induction case.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, p. 50, the a=1 case.

proof.text: If $a=0$, the model gives $\alpha\in L$ with $|\alpha^p+v|<s$. Set $v^\prime=-\alpha^p$ and $K^\prime=k(v^\prime)^\wedge$. Because every element of the algebraically closed $k$ is a $p$th power, $s=\inf_{c\in K}|c^p+v|\le r:=\inf_{c\in k}|v-c|$. Thus $\delta:=|v-v^\prime|<s\le r$. For each $c\in k$ we have $|v-v^\prime|<|v-c|$, so the ultrametric inequality gives $|v^\prime-c|=|v-c|$; in particular $v^\prime\notin k$ and its distance infimum is also $r$. Since $|p|\le1$, $|pv^\prime|\le\max(|pv|,|p|\delta)<s\le r$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, p. 50, the a=0 case; perfectness of the ground field simplifies the distance comparison.

proof.text: The substitution $v\mapsto v^\prime$ defines an isometric $k$-isomorphism $\phi:K\to K^\prime$ close to the inclusions in $L$, as follows. Both $v,v^\prime$ are transcendental over algebraically closed $k$. Choose a real $c_0$ with $\delta/r<c_0<1$. For a linear factor $T-c$, $|v-v^\prime|\le (\delta/r)|v-c|$. If two nonzero values have this relative error bound, their norms agree; multiplying two such comparisons preserves the same bound by the ultrametric inequality. Inversion preserves it because $|x^{-1}-x^{\prime-1}|=|x-x^\prime|/(|x||x^\prime|)$. Factoring numerators and denominators over $k$ therefore proves $|f(v)-f(v^\prime)|\le (\delta/r)|f(v)|$ and equality of norms for every rational function $f$. Extend substitution and its inverse to the closures by sending Cauchy sequences to their limits. Isometry makes the maps well-defined and mutually inverse; passing to limits gives $|u-\phi(u)|\le c_0|u|$ for all $u\in K$. Apply [lem-trf-analytic-close-embedding-degree] to $K\hookrightarrow L$ and $K\xrightarrow{\phi}K^\prime\hookrightarrow L$, obtaining $[L:K^\prime]=[L:K]=p$.

source.place: Lemmas 6.3.2–6.3.3, printed p. 48, applied in the proof of Theorem 6.3.1 on p. 50; rational-factor calculation written out.

proof.text:
The field $K^\prime$ is complete and immediate over $k$ and $K^\prime=k(v^\prime)^\wedge$. The bound $|p(-v^\prime)|<r=\inf_{c\in k}|-v^\prime-c|$ permits [lem-trf-analytic-pth-root-obstruction], applied to the coordinate $-v^\prime$, whose rational closure equals $K^\prime$. It shows that $-v^\prime$ has no $p$th root in $K^\prime$. Hence [lem-trf-prime-binomial-irreducible] makes $T^p+v^\prime$ irreducible over $K^\prime$, including in mixed characteristic. Its root $\alpha$ consequently generates a subextension of degree $p$ in $L/K^\prime$, which already has degree $p$; thus $K^\prime(\alpha)=L$. Put $H=k(\alpha)^\wedge\subset L$. Since $v^\prime=-\alpha^p$, the closed field $H$ contains $K^\prime$ and $\alpha$, so it contains $L$ and equals it. Also $\alpha
otin k$, since $v^\prime
otin k$. This completes the induction step for $a=0$. At $i=n$ the induction supplies $E=k(z_n)^\wedge$ with $z_n
otin k$, as required.
